summary:
# NOTES: *Shoulder to Shoulder* by Gordon Stables (Dr. Gordon Stables, M.D., C.M., Surgeon RN). Story of the stirring times of old, narrated by grandson "Williamie" to his grandfather "Auld-da" (Ian/John Robertson). Single book with three Books (I, II, III), each with numbered chapters. Frontispiece: "Hurrah, my lads; remember Egypt!" shouted Sir John Moore (p. 310). Epigraph: Burns, "Be Britain still to Britain true..."

Narrator framing: narrator sits on a "creepie" (low stool) by Auld-da's knee in winter twilight. Auld-da's cottage: "but and a ben," near Bass o' Ury, Inverurie area (Ury river). Auld-da died aged 89; last words to narrator: "Don't I know my own laddie! Mercy! Mercy!" Auld-da read the Bible yearly and "Looking unto Jesus." Auld-da collected half-pay in Aberdeen every quarter day, walked, brought apples (codlin) and nuts; narrator and sister Leonora ("Sissie") met him; he gave each a half-crown. Auld-da was skilled with claymore (cut through door-edge trick; sharpened scythes). Narrator's father sang "He's owre the hills that I lo'e weel"; mother crooned Jacobite songs; narrator was a "little rebel" aged 7 for Bonnie Prince Charlie; narrator admits Jacobite sympathy but loves Queen Victoria. Narrator's ancestors: Gordons (father's side) fought for Charles; mother's side Robertsons of the Braes of R----, royalists, fought at Culloden in 1st Royal Scots (Pontius Pilate's Guards). Duke of Kent was Auld-da's colonel and saved his life; Auld-da once talked with the young Princess (Victoria) as a baby. Duke of Cumberland ("bloody Duke") anecdote: ordered shooting of a dying Highlander; English officer refused ("I am your humble servant, but not your executioner"); Cumberland shot him himself.

**Book I: In the Highlands a Hundred Years Ago**
- Ch I–II: Above.
- Ch III: Auld-da's tale. Grandfather's father's father (Robertson) lived near Beauly (river Beauly, Belladrum castle of Lord Lovat, cousin Simon Fraser). Lived to 101, found dead against pine with snuff-box. Fiona Stuart (Robertson's sister-in-law), 18, dark-brown eyes, raven hair, called "Gipsy"; sweetheart Ian Robertson (soldier, 1st Royals, abroad). Raoul McIvor "Raoul Dhu"/Black Ronald, musician, Lovat's companion, tall, rake. Offered to buy deerhound; Fiona refused. Brother-in-law (Robertson) scolded him for drinking water not sitting. Raoul shot a hare; Fiona bent over dying hare. Raoul demanded marriage; Fiona refused ("ma ghaol ma chree" for Ian). Raoul threatened to dirk Ian. Raoul seized her arm; dwarf MUIRACHIE leapt on his back and choked him unconscious. Muirachie: speaks broken English ("ta rascal Raoul Dhu no pe deaded"). Collie dog Kooran.
- Ch IV: Fontenoy (1745; Cumberland; Marshal Saxe; Dutch cowards; Royal Scots). Raoul Dhu refused fiery cross; Robertson refused to follow Charles ("I'll follow no cross save that which our Saviour carried"); threat to Robertson's family. Muirachie warned of Raoul. Robertson farm fortified; ten men incl. Muirachie. Battle of Culloden; Raoul returned bloody, revelling in Beauly; Muirachie spied and warned Robertson. Muirachie hid women/children in Corney's Cave (whisky-still ravine, "Corney's Cave"). Fiona rode/walked fourteen miles to Culloden camp at night; gave water to wounded soldier in bonnet; fought a rebel with claymore; sentry at camp; reached tent of Captain McDonald; Ian present. "To horse! to horse!" Thirty men.
- Ch V: Raid at farm; Raoul Dhu attacked; Mrs. Robertson (Mary) and children prayed; dog Kooran; Robertson fought with claymores; fire in copse; Muirachie saved women from fire. Battering-ram; last trench; red-coats arrived; Raoul's men slain; Ian and Raoul fought; Ian's sword pierced Raoul; Fiona begged mercy; Ian sheathed sword. Raoul taken prisoner, hanged at Edinburgh. Ian married Fiona. Farm burned; Muirachie died saving cattle. Narrator's father and uncle Peter born. Narrator's grandfather (the boy Ian) born ~35 years later at Forest Farm/Braes of R----, Ian born there; omens: four magpies, deer ate oats, raven, sour cream.
- Ch VI: Narrator's visit to Deeside; Miss Steelyard (old maid, "I hate boys"; "dangle at the end of a long rope"); village minister tea. Ian's school: Dominie Freeschal (thin, tawse, tawse-bowler). Ian renamed "Sir John Robertson" by the boys; rhyme "Sir John Robertson is my name... Forest Farm's my happy home." Tawse ("pandé"). Boy-cruelties: Ian drew caricatures, got boys tawsed.
- Ch VII: Mrs. Freeschal (plain fair-haired, sinewy; Mrs. Nairn beat dominie with broom-handle for son Johnnie Nairn); Tonal (Robertson pupil, "believe/deceive/relieve") and Tonal's father Mr. Young complaint; Rachel Freeschal (age 8, fair hair, blue eyes, bare legs, "little queen"); Kenneth McRae; Ian called Rachel "little wretch," kept in after hours; Rachel passed sugar-bools and brandy-snaps through broken window; Ian climbed chimney, stuck fast, slept, escaped; dominie fainted at ghost (Ian black from soot, barn-owl cry); Ian kicked dominie's hat; bath in burn.
- Ch VIII: Conspirators Tonal and Ian; tawse burned in forest fire; feast with trout; Tonal to be soldier ("drum-major"); Ian: farmer with sheep as many as pines, marry Rachel. Tonal enlisted; dominie bought new tawse; cock-fight at Christmas (Ian crowned king of school); Reel of Tulloch with Rachel (Fraser tartan frock); Tom Grahame threat; fight in forest — Ian's kilt pin in Tom's chest, nickname "Preen Mhor" (big pin); Tom bed for a month; friendship. Dominie's visit; school ends; Rachel's farewell at peat-stack.
- Ch IX: Leaving home at 15 with 5 shillings; Rachel waved from peat-stack; prayer in pine wood. Staymaker Mr. Craig in High Street, Inverness (cat, wife, rats). Mrs. Fraser; Lodge at Falkirk Lodge on Ness; Cousin Captain Fraser (haughty, Black Watch). Dog Dash (collie). Shilling; enlisted in 1st Royals (butler: "And he's going to fight the French"). "I will not serve under a Fraser of Lovat... I am a Robertson and a loyalist."
- Ch X: Threw King's shilling in sea (with Dash); fisherman's hut at Beauly; visit to parents; Rachel's warning; soldiers came; Corney's Cave hideout; gillie brought food; captured in copse; Ellen (inn at Beauly) drugged soldiers, freed Ian; "Pretend to sleep, fly when I put out the lights."
- Ch XI: Dominie's letter; Rachel's note with four-bladed clover ("trust more in God than even the four-bladed clover"); Ellen; three Forty-second soldiers; McGregor sergeant's humiliation (blackened faces, muskets up chimney); John Chisholm lawyer, Inverness ("go be shot like a good boy"); Fort George; recruiting sergeant (powdered cue); enlisted as "Private John Robertson, of the 1st Royals" — name John.

**Book II: Off to Join His Regiment**
- Ch I: Fort George drill; Sergeant Brown; Captain Drake (beautiful fist; "Don't soil your gloves"); Lady Jane ("love of a lad"); bayonet exercise; sword lessons promised; recruits McGruer and Pope fight (Pope's nose; Playfair); Vengeful packet ship from Inverness to Leith in December.
- Ch II: Storm; cattle and sheep thrown overboard; sailor lost; five days to Leith; Edinburgh Castle.
- Ch III: Captain Drake lent books; Dr. McLeod (giant surgeon) danced sword-dance; hornpipe on dinner-table wager (five shillings); Major Lloyd; Blood vs McLeod (Miss Niven; thrown through window); O'Reilly (Irish, challenge to Drake; Major Jones Welsh second; Blood second); duel in park; Blood wore stays; Drake's note "Thine to the spine, Patrick O'Reilly."
- Ch IV: Drake's story of Revolution: 1792; Louis XVI; Tuileries; Danton; Brunswick proclamation of 25 July; Sept massacres; war with France Feb 1793; Dumouriez.
- Ch V: Toulon 1793 (Lord Hood; Napoleon's artillery); Corsica; Bastia 22 May; brigands rescue (Drake stripped, rescued by McLeod & O'Reilly); Calvi storming, Morello tower, Royals.
- Ch VI: Ian promoted corporal, then sergeant; Freemason; Tom Grahame reunion; drunk ride; colonel W----, of 42nd; ribbon; promise to Colonel. Quiberon 1795 massacre; Napoleon in Italy; Lodi.
- Ch VII: Napoleon's ambition; Campo Formio; Ireland rebellion 1798; Humbert at Killala; Lake; Cornwallis; Dr. McNiven; flotilla Sallenelle; Royal Navy; coalition.
- Ch VIII: Furlough 1801; Craig dead; Lodge deserted (Frasers gone, Captain fled to fight for Charlie); Ellen tells Rachel dead; Dash alive; Dash; "Hame is hame"; Aboukir 1801; Drake falls; Tom Grahame's "Shoulder to shoulder"; Alexandria 21 March 1801; Captain Fraser dies; "Ailie" daughter; sergeant promotion (colour-sergeant).

**Book III: From War to Gentle Peace**
- Ch I: Ramsgate 1801; Duke of Kent (Royal Highness); gull ("Sir, this is not sport—it is murder!"); flea anecdote; flogging; malingerers; Tonal (Dominie's pupil, now bandmaster) "Miller o' Drone" played in church.
- Ch II: Gibraltar 1802; Duke of Kent; reforms; Spanish stiletto stab; vendetta; "Put not your trust in princes."
- Ch III: Mr. Myers murder box; Milan conspirators; masked figure; mutiny Christmas Eve 1802; note "Your Major Drake... murdered"; Blood not found; O'Reilly mistaken for Duke; McLeod.
- Ch IV: Dying soldier confesses; 26 Dec 1802 second mutiny; ten court-martialed; Reilly shot; Napoleon's Duke of Enghien execution 1804.
- Ch V: Trafalgar 1805; Ulm; Blood killed in battle; Jones lost leg; Ian's scar on left shoulder ("Only a scratch"); Drake recruitment at Dundalk; Duke's promise of Highland battalion ensign; Tonal reunion; Mrs. Stapleton & Eleanor (Nora/Ellen) at Booterstown.
- Ch VI: Dundalk fair; skipper St. Patrick (Eleanor's brother); recruits 19; Copenhagen bombardment 1807 (McLeod, Drake, O'Reilly); marriage to Eleanor (Ellen) Presbyterian; Killarney honeymoon; song "Kate Kearney."
- Ch VII: Peninsula; Junot Portugal; Murat Madrid; Loison at Evora; Sir Arthur Wellesley; Sir John Moore's retreat from Salamanca; Frere; Morla; Astorga; Napoleon leaves 1 Jan 1809.
- Ch VIII: Retreat; Tom Grahame's orphan baby Annie; Spanish girl nurse; Tonal wounded (pipes shot through); "Death or victory."
- Ch IX: Corunna 16 Jan 1809; Moore's death ("Hurrah! my lads; remember Egypt!"); Tom carries Moore; buried at night (Wolfe's poem); Tonal married at Dover + bagpipes.
- Ch X: Ellen follows soldier; Bergen-op-Zoom 1814; cat on ship; Robert born on battlefield; Ellen kills harpy with pistol; cannon-ball stocking; Danube ice.
- Ch XI: Salamanca transport to Canada 1813; women's inspection (Ellen with pike); Anticosti shipwreck; War of 1812; Chippewa; Walcott quote; "Hands across the water."
- Ch XII: Canada; Red-Eye Micmac chief; little Mary (mother, born c. 1814-15) and Red-Eye; humming-bird; bear fight (O'Reilly shot bear); Duke's promise via H----; Tonal's Spanish wife; Mary and Tonal taken.
- Ch XIII: McLeod's report; Roberts killed; Red-Eye with scalp; Red-Eye's past (Meemee, Grat Pike); march in moonlight; Red-Eye's prayer.
- Ch XIV: Attack on Micmac camp; Red-Eye dies ("Lead me through the darkness... to the land of the Great White Spirit"); grave; peace; Waterloo missed (transport on sandbank a week); grandfather, Tom, Tonal retire; McLeod in Glasgow; Napoleon at St Helena, grave; pink flowers stolen from H.M.S. Valorous; "So sinks the pride of former days."

THE END.
